blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Write a PETZAAL Point and Evidence for: 'How does the opening create a sense of chaos?'
questions.a: For example: Point: Shakespeare opens with chaos to grab the audience. Evidence: the nobles are ordered below deck and the ship splits.
questions.model: Point: Shakespeare opens the play in chaos so the audience is gripped at once. | Evidence: the Boatswain orders the nobles 'To cabin!' | Technique: imperatives (commands) | Zoom in: 'cabin' sends a king below like a passenger | Analyse: the normal order of power is reversed | Alternative: it may also show the Boatswain's courage | Link: so the opening asks who really holds power.

questions.q: Predict: who might have caused the storm, and why? Give one clue.
questions.a: Prospero, using magic, to bring his enemies to the island; clue: the title and the island characters list.

questions.q: in the portal response box, write one PETZAAL paragraph: 'How does Shakespeare show that a storm can make kings powerless?' Starter: 'Shakespeare shows...'
questions.a: A PETZAAL paragraph using the Boatswain's question, zooming in on 'roarers' or 'name of king'.
questions.model: Point: Shakespeare shows that a storm makes a king powerless. | Evidence: 'What cares these roarers for the name of king?' | Technique: rhetorical question | Zoom in: 'name' suggests a title is only a word | Analyse: nature cannot be commanded, so rank means nothing | Alternative: the Boatswain may also be angry at idle nobles | Link: this prepares us for Prospero, who can command storms.

questions.q: add one sentence on how the audience might feel watching this scene.
questions.a: For example: The audience would feel tense and curious, because the ship seems lost so early.

questions.q: why might Shakespeare start with action, not explanation?
questions.a: To hook the audience; the explanation comes in scene 2 (exposition).

questions.q: Answer the ponder: is a storm that ignores rank frightening or fair?
questions.a: Answers vary, e.g. both: it is terrifying, but it shows all people are equal in the face of nature.
